storyOverrides.title: Behold a Pale Horse.
storyOverrides.deck: A Josh King exclusive on the most controversial account on X: Behold a Pale Horse
storyOverrides.author: Corey Becker
storyOverrides.label: What if everything we thought we knew was never what it seemed?
storyOverrides.body:
**BEHOLD A PALE HORSE**

*What if everything we thought we knew was never what it seemed?* 

Horse is a man that so many of us fight the urge to become.

Maybe it’s because, deep inside, we have trust issues that won’t allow us to see beyond the veil. Or perhaps it’s something far more unsettling: the inability to accept that the things we’ve always known to be true may, in fact, be false.

I think it’s only right to say that when it comes to *Behold a Pale Horse*, you should understand one thing.

**Behold.**

This is not for the weak-minded.

It’s not for the sheep.

This is for those who have always had a hunch. Those who have questioned whether the sports they hold so dear to their hearts, the same sports woven into the fabric of their childhoods, their memories, and their very identities, may not be everything they’ve been led to believe.

That these outcomes may be…

***Predetermined.***

Have they always been? Who knows?

And perhaps that’s the most disturbing part of it all. Not knowing. Never knowing. Being forced to question something you’ve spent your entire life believing was beyond question.

But what we do know is that since the rise of mobile sports betting, and with the introduction of readily accessible player props, we’ve witnessed a shift in the culture of sports.

You can no longer turn on the television and check a score without knowing what the line is.

Those days are in the past.

And in the present?

**They play in our faces.**

They allow us to believe we’re smarter than we actually are.

And that’s not to say we aren’t educated individuals, capable of making educated guesses. Because that’s precisely what sports betting is.

An educated guess.

But there are too many times when we find ourselves being convinced to bet a certain way. Nudged toward a particular outcome. Led to believe that a conclusion was ours to arrive at, when perhaps the path had already been laid before us.

It’s almost magic, in a sense, how effortlessly they’re able to sway public opinion.

But it’s no different from the voting polls.

The only difference is that there is no time limit on this.

This isn’t the stock market.

The books are open 24 hours a day. Seven days a week. Three hundred and sixty-five days a year.

They’re always there.

Watching. Waiting. Offering us the illusion of an opportunity.

For better or for worse?

**Absolutely not.**

Because somewhere between the numbers, the lines, the narratives, and the outcomes, there exists a question that most would rather never ask.

What if the very things we’ve spent our lives studying, defending, and believing in were never quite what we thought they were?

And what if the reason we refuse to entertain that possibility isn’t because the evidence is absent…

But because accepting it would mean questioning everything?

Not many have dared to challenge the wickedness that some believe has been bestowed upon us.

*Behold a Pale Horse* is one of the few.

Everybody takes the money.

Or at least, that’s what we’ve been conditioned to believe.

And perhaps that’s the problem.

**We no longer know what to believe.**

Are the personalities we see plastered across these gambling channels real? Are they plants? Who are these people? What’s their background? And why does it sometimes seem so difficult to find out?

Are we watching independent minds give independent opinions? Or are we watching something else entirely?

I don’t know.

And neither do you.

But I’ve had the pleasure of speaking with Horse, one on one.

And we see things through the same prism, as he would say.

I find what he’s doing inspiring.

It’s courageous.

And, in a sense, it’s crazy.

Not crazy because I believe he’s wrong.

But crazy because of what he’s willing to put on the line.

His reputation. His credibility. His willingness to be ridiculed by the very people he hopes to enlighten.

And perhaps the greatest irony of it all? The very man questioning the machine is sitting atop the Westgate SuperContest leaderboard under a name that couldn't be more fitting: *RIGGEDNFL-1.* 

Make of that what you will.

You see, I get the feeling that Horse does all of this in an effort to pay it forward. To share the knowledge he’s acquired. To question the puppet masters and call attention to what he believes are their money-harvesting practices.

That’s not an easy thing to do.

Especially in a world where questioning the narrative is often enough to have your own credibility questioned.

Where skepticism is mistaken for ignorance, and the desire to understand is sometimes treated as a refusal to accept reality.

But whose reality?

Theirs?

Ours?

Or the one we’ve all quietly agreed to live in because the alternative is simply too uncomfortable to entertain?

I feel blessed, and strangely more at ease, since meeting Horse.

Not because he’s given me all the answers.

But because he’s reminded me that I’m not crazy for asking the questions.

There’s comfort in that. In realizing that somewhere, beyond the noise, beyond the lines and the endless parade of personalities telling us what to think, there are others looking through that same prism.

Others who have seen enough to question what they’re being shown.

And still, the uncertainty remains.

Because sometimes the veil slips back over all of our eyes.

And we return to bliss.

We watch the games. We cheer for our teams. We remember what it felt like to be children, when the only thing that mattered was the final score.

When a touchdown was just a touchdown.

When a missed field goal was just a missed field goal.

When the improbable was simply that.

Improbable.

And perhaps that’s the cruelest part of questioning it all.

The possibility that innocence, once lost, cannot be reclaimed.

Because sometimes…

**What we see, we cannot unsee.**

And what we know, or believe we know, we cannot simply choose to unknow.

This is not a declaration of certainty.

Quite the opposite.

This is the story of uncertainty. Of suspicion. Of the uncomfortable space between what we know, what we’re told, and what we’re willing to believe.

It’s about a man willing to ask the questions that so many of us have spent our lives trying to silence.

And perhaps, more importantly, it’s about what happens when we finally find the courage to ask them ourselves.

This is the story of *Behold a Pale Horse*.

***Watch Josh King's exclusive interview with Behold a Pale Horse, and decide for yourself what lies beyond the veil.***
